class_guess: Skelet 1-like: multi-level counter on phase defects between inert fossil blocks (x3 per epoch)
summary: Multi-level counter on 00/11 defects between inert fossil blocks; a new fossil 3F+72 cells long each epoch.
mechanism: The tape is alternating cells with isolated defects (00 or 11). Sweeps flip every pair. A leftward head turns at a 00 in D-phase (E reads 0) or at an 11 in E-phase (C reads 1). A rightward head turns only at a 00 in B-phase (C reads 0), so the phase decides pass or turn.

Level 1: the head bounces between the right edge and a wall W that moves 1 cell per hit (E-turn 00 at x -> 11 at x-1, C-turn 11 at x -> 00 at x-1; 554/555 single-turn trips to 3e6). W eats the active block X while the right block Y grows by about 1.7 cells per trip.

Deeper trips stop at the defects between fossil blocks, which cycle through 2 or 3 positions (e.g. 180 -> 179 -> 178 -> 180), and at the left end. This is a mixed-radix counter, and each overflow ends a phase. There are 3 phases per epoch: X grows, then Y grows, then W eats X and Y freezes into a fossil.

Epoch laws, exact on every epoch from blank to 2e10 steps: fossils F = 2736 -> 8280 -> 24912 -> 74808 cells (F' = 3F + 72); mid blocks X = 248 -> 752 -> 2264 -> 6800 (X' = 3X + 8). There are 3 left records per epoch (3 cells each), and each epoch takes 9.04x longer than the one before.

Fossil lengths are inert mod 4. Inserting 4j cells into any block (fossils or X) leaves the run unchanged except for those lengths (4/4 starts, to 3.5e9 steps, the new blocks are identical). Inserting 2 mod 4 cells changes the run (3/3; one ran off a 2^25-cell tape).
Halting needs `C> 111` or `A> 11`, i.e. two adjacent defects in the wrong phase. The run has no halt to 2e10 steps, and neither sibling halts to 2e9.

template.diff: different table (4-5 transitions from #11/#33 under the best renaming); no shared rules
template.note: Nearest proved neighbour: our kill #11 (Sk1C2, SBCv6 TM21 architecture). Its .v has one counter level: shift lemmas S1-S6, window lemmas T1-T14, digit lemmas Lb/Lf/Rb/Ro, the rules M_spec / Mdrop_spec / O_spec, and an abstract INV over one digit list. W4-3 matches only the bottom layer (sweep and turn lemmas). Its counter has unboundedly many levels: fossil defects with 2-3 states, the 3-phase epoch and the left-end counter, and #11 has no analogue of these. The closest open cases are #32/R4 (multi-level counter, parked).

strategy: Build an exact abstract model at the defect level: turn/pass/reset rules by phase, the wall trip, and fossils kept only mod 4. Check that it reproduces every trip to 1e9, then look for a recursive invariant over the fossil list (epoch = 3 counter overflows). Siblings 512/588 would then need only a new init.
risks: The phase rule is not derived yet: which defects turn, pass or reset depends on the head's phase. The left-end region (a small counter that grows 3 cells per phase) is not ruled.
A proof needs a recursive multi-level invariant with no template (the same shape as #32/R4, parked). Expect several stages.
Residues mod 4 matter: a block of the wrong residue changes the run (one perturbed start ran off the tape), so the invariant must pin every fossil residue.

checkpoint_questions.text: Fig 2: does the head bounce between the right edge and a wall that creeps left (the short wedge tips near the middle), with a longer excursion to the left every few trips?
Fig 3: do the sampled columns show flat bands (old blocks) that keep their edges, while a new, wider band opens at the right?
Fund one ~2 h stage to derive the phase rule and an exact defect-level model (recommended), or park W4-3 with #32/R4 as a multi-level counter?
